free-guides.big: I'm neurodivergent, and I run a very small shop called Frog Logic from my lounge.

free-guides.small: Twenty-three short guides — autism, ADHD, AuDHD, dyslexia, dyspraxia, PDA, OCD and the rest — in plain English.

free-guides.big:
The person it's about.
AND the people around them.
free-guides.small: The partner. The manager. The mum who still says “but you don't look autistic.”

free-guides.big:
No email address.
No sign-up.
Nothing to tick.
free-guides.small: Download the one you need and send it to whoever needs to read it. That's the whole idea.

planner.big: Every planner I've ever bought was built for someone else's brain.

Hourly grids I never filled in.
Habit trackers that became a record of failure by February.
planner.small: “Just write it down” — yes, but where, and in what order, and why does the page assume my day starts at 6am?

planner.tag: so I built one that asks first
planner.big: Fifteen questions about how your day actually runs.
planner.small: What you keep forgetting. What a hard day looks like for you. What actually helps.

planner.big: A planner is built from your answers and emailed to you as a PDF.
planner.small: Your own words are on the pages. There's a hard-day page you can tear in half and hand to someone.

planner.big: If it doesn't fit, answer again and it gets rebuilt free.

honesty-post.big: Because I think people like to know.
Every bit of this shop was made by one neurodivergent person with a PC.
honesty-post.small: And a lot of help from an AI that does the coding and gets overruled regularly.
That's normal this early, apparently. I'm not going anywhere.

honesty-post.big:
If you've ever thought
“I wish someone made a ___ for brains like mine”
honesty-post.small: I would really like to hear it. The best things in the shop came from exactly that sentence.

honesty-post.big: No idea is too small or too specific.

when-words-go.tag: I made a card that says
when-words-go.big:
“I can't speak right now.
I can hear you.
Please give me a minute.”
Twenty-two point-and-show cards for the moment speech leaves.
when-words-go.small: For when you're stood in a shop, or a GP's waiting room, and it's gone.
With blanks to write your own.

when-words-go.big: I made it because I needed it.
£3. Print it at home. Laminate it if you can.
